documents.title: Acute Visit: Diarrhea After Travel
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning, seen same day. 28M got back 2 days ago from a week in southern Mexico. On his last day there he developed sudden watery diarrhea that has kept getting worse: no blood, like water, large volumes, about 12 times a day at its worst. Some nausea and cramping in his legs. No fever, no vomiting, no belly pain. No antibiotics recently and he has not taken anything for it. Did not get any travel vaccines before going. Ate a lot from street stalls and drank tap water when he couldn't find bottled.

PMH: exertional rhabdomyolysis with AKI August 2024, resolved. No meds. NKDA.

Exam: tired but alert. HR 102, rest of vitals normal. Mucous membranes a bit dry. Bowel sounds hyperactive, abdomen soft and nontender.

Stat labs back during the visit: Na 133, K 3.1, bicarb 18, Cr 1.3. Stool microscopy: no fecal WBCs, no blood.

A/P: Acute high-volume watery diarrhea after travel with volume depletion and low potassium and bicarbonate. Picture fits cholera; treating presumptively.
- Oral rehydration solution, aiming to match losses: at least a liter for every few stools, sipping steadily. Packets from the pharmacy; recipe given as backup.
- Doxycycline 300 mg as a single dose today.
- Potassium chloride 20 mEq twice daily for 3 days.
- Stool culture sent.
- Return or go to the ED if he can't keep up with fluids, gets dizzy on standing, or urine output drops; with his kidney history we want to stay ahead of this.
- RN call tomorrow; repeat BMP early next week.

documents.title: Follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called to check in. Took the doxycycline yesterday afternoon, keeping it down. Stools down to about 5 overnight and this morning, still watery but less volume. Drinking ORS steadily, urinating regularly, light yellow. No dizziness. Taking potassium. Reviewed return precautions. Lab appointment Tuesday 3/4.

documents.title: Stool culture
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Stool culture grew Vibrio cholerae O1, confirming cholera. Already treated. Lab has reported to the state health department as required; they may call him. Patient notified via portal.

documents.title: Your stool culture
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi August, your culture confirmed cholera, which is what we treated you for. It's a reportable infection, so the state health department may reach out with a few questions. Good hand washing at home, and keep up the fluids until things are back to normal. See you for labs tomorrow.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs are all back to normal: sodium 139, potassium 4.0, bicarbonate 24, creatinine 0.98. Glad the diarrhea has stopped. Your potassium course is finished, nothing more to take. Nothing further needed.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks! Back to normal since Sunday. Health dept called yesterday, all set.

documents.title: Summer race question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'm signed up for a 50K in July. After last August is there anything I should do differently or any reason I shouldn't?

documents.title: RE: Summer race question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No reason not to. Your kidneys and muscle enzymes recovered fully. Same plan we discussed: train in the heat gradually, drink to thirst plus salt on long efforts, back off when the temperature climbs, and stop and get help if you feel lightheaded or your urine goes dark or scant afterward.

documents.title: Annual Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Ran a 50K in July without problems, kept the pace easy in the heat. No GI issues since the cholera in February. Work steady.

PMH: exertional rhabdomyolysis with AKI 8/2024, resolved. Cholera 2/2025 after travel to Mexico, culture-confirmed, resolved. Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker; alcohol rare.
PHQ-2 0.

Exam: well, fit. Vitals normal. HEENT, neck, heart, lungs, abdomen, skin and extremities normal.

A/P: Healthy adult.
- Flu vaccine today. Plans COVID shot at his pharmacy.
- Screening up to date for age. Return in a year.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy reports COVID-19 vaccine (Moderna, 2025-2026 formula) given 10/19/2025, right deltoid. Added to immunization history.

events.reason: Profuse watery diarrhea after travel to Bangladesh

results.test: Bacteria identified in Stool by Culture

medications.sig: Take 4 tablets (1 g) by mouth once

documents.title: Emergency Department Note with Observation Course
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
29M, healthy, flew home two days ago from two weeks volunteering on flood relief in a rural coastal village in Bangladesh. Since yesterday more than 15 stools, thin, pale and odorless, rice-water in appearance. No abdominal pain, no fever, no blood. Lightheaded when he stands and has barely urinated. Ate street food and drank untreated water there. Prior cholera after a trip to Mexico in February 2025 and exertional rhabdomyolysis in August 2024. No medications. NKDA.

Triage: BP 86/52, HR 128, T 37.1 C, RR 20, SpO2 98% RA.
Exam: tired, alert. Skin tents, mucous membranes dry. Tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, active bowel sounds.

Labs: Na 134, K 2.9, HCO3 15, BUN 38, Cr 1.9.

Impression: cholera with severe dehydration, hypokalemia, metabolic acidosis and prerenal acute kidney injury.

Course: Two large-bore IVs. Balanced crystalloid boluses started at once, then continued at a rate matched to stool output; IV potassium chloride, then oral potassium once taking fluids. Azithromycin 1 g PO given. Stool culture sent. Placed in ED observation overnight. Stool output slowed markedly by evening; drinking ORS on his own by midnight; urinating well.

Morning 2/22: BP 112/70, HR 84. Cr 1.1, K 3.6. Tolerating fluids and food.

Disposition: discharged home. Continue oral rehydration solution to match losses. See PCP this week for BMP. Return for dizziness, falling urine output or diarrhea he can't keep up with.

Addendum 2/23: stool culture Vibrio cholerae O1. Reported to public health.

documents.title: Post-ED follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record received this morning. Called patient. Home since Sunday morning. Two loose stools yesterday, none today so far. Drinking well, urine normal. No lightheadedness. Visit with PCP Wednesday 2/25 with BMP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after ED and overnight observation 2/21 to 2/22 for cholera after relief work in Bangladesh. ED record reviewed: BP 86/52, HR 128 on arrival; Na 134, K 2.9, HCO3 15, Cr 1.9; IV crystalloid and potassium, azithromycin 1 g. Cr 1.1 and K 3.6 at discharge. Stool culture Vibrio cholerae O1.

Today: stools formed since Monday, eating and drinking normally, no dizziness. Back at work remotely.

Exam: well-appearing. Vitals normal. Mucous membranes moist. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P: Cholera with dehydration and AKI, clinically resolved. BMP today; expect normal.
This is his second episode in a year. Return as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood work is back to normal: potassium 4.1, bicarbonate 23, creatinine 1.0. You're all set.

documents.title: Vaccine record
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Could you send me my immunization history? A race I signed up for wants one with my entry.

documents.title: RE: Vaccine record
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Your immunization record is now in your documents tab. Let us know if they need it in a different format.
